Duration::nanoseconds¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

Series Duration::nanoseconds() const

The Sub-Microsecond Field¶

nanoseconds() extracts the final three digits of the normalized decomposition, so every valid result lies in 0..999. It is not the Duration’s complete nanosecond count. Use total().nanoseconds() for that conversion or host() when an exact owning std::vector<std::int64_t> is required.

The distinction is substantial: a value of 1'000'000'007 ns has nanosecond component 7, while its total is 1'000'000'007. Because this method uses integer remainder arithmetic, it preserves the final digits exactly even for magnitudes beyond floating-point integer precision. Floor normalization makes the component of -1 ns equal to 999, paired with the preceding fields of -1 day, 23:59:59.999999.

Result Contract¶

The method returns a new shape-preserving Int64 Series, maps NaT to Duration::kNaT, and supports scalar through rank-three and zero-element inputs. It is O(numel) and does not mutate or reinterpret the source.

Examples¶

Example 1. Recover the final three decimal digits exactly.

std::cout << pluss::series::print(
    pluss::duration::nanos(93'784'005'006'007LL).nanoseconds());

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=7

Example 2. The last nanosecond before zero has component 999.

constexpr std::int64_t hour = 3'600'000'000'000LL;
constexpr std::int64_t day = 86'400'000'000'000LL;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(
    pluss::duration::nanos({-1, -hour, -day}).nanoseconds());

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[999, 0, 0]

Example 3. Matrix structure and absence are retained exactly.

auto values = pluss::duration::nanos(
    {93'784'005'006'007LL, pluss::Duration::kNaT, -1, 0}, {2,2});
std::cout << pluss::series::print(values.nanoseconds());

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡   7 -9223372036854775808 ⎤
⎣ 999                    0 ⎦

Example 4. Empty arrays retain shape without producing lane values.

std::cout << pluss::series::print(
    pluss::duration::zeros({2,0,3}).nanoseconds());

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,0,3], strides=[0,3,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=0, contiguous=true)
[]

See Also¶

  • microseconds(): the preceding three-digit field.

  • total().nanoseconds(): the complete elapsed count as Series.

  • host(): exact owning host extraction without a Series conversion.
